feedback.answered: A1: the leader assigns current-term log indexes, gathers per-voter match values including witnesses but excluding observers, selects the quorum match index and invokes log.tryCommit with its current term. A2: campaigning increments term and votes for self; transition reset clears vote responses, pending ReadIndex support and remote match state, while retaining log history; incoming term handling rejects lower-term protocol traffic and transitions on higher terms, with a recent-leader vote suppression exception. These relationships connect through current-term commit qualification and fresh support after authority changes. ReadIndex requires a current-term committed entry for a multi-voter cluster, records request context and origin, and uses heartbeat confirmations. The apparent observer counting concern has producer counterevidence: nonzero read contexts are sent only to votingMembers, and observers receive zero-context ordinary heartbeats; normal observer replies therefore do not supply a pending read context. A separate source discrepancy remains: readIndex.confirm returns and removes all queued statuses through the confirmed context, but handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation uses each status context only for local completions; every remote reply uses the triggering heartbeat context rather than that status context. Follower response handling preserves the received context, and pendingReadIndex.addReady indexes batches by exact context. This is a correlation question, not yet an execution finding.

Inspect alternative retransmission, drop and timeout consumers before inferring lost automatic continuation or any end-to-end read consequence.

formation.explanation: Leader proposals become indexed current-term entries; follower predecessor checks and durable-before-response dispatch produce replication support. Leader counts voters including witnesses, selects quorum match and commits only a current-term entry, then propagates commit. Replication rejects retry with a decreased next index and compacted peers use snapshots. Committed entries enter apply queues; application callbacks complete proposals and allow confirmed reads once locally applied. ReadIndex separately collects current-leader heartbeat quorum after a current-term commit.

context.explanation: Ticks on eligible nonleaders initiate election after applied history catches up. Candidate increments term, self-votes and wins a voter quorum; vote grant checks history and prior vote. Known response filtering precedes raft dispatch. Higher terms reset role state; stale protocol messages are dropped, with recent-leader vote suppression. Leadership acquisition appends no-op; CheckQuorum can revoke authority. Transfer pauses proposals and requests target election after catch-up. Membership applies via RSM and snapshots restore application plus membership.

connection.explanation: Committed history survives authority change and constrains subsequent elections and append replacement. Transition reset removes prior vote counts, remote match support and pending read confirmations; new leader commits a current-term entry before multi-voter reads. Applied membership determines voters, witnesses and observers; campaigning with unapplied committed entries is suppressed. Old network responses face term and known-member checks; old read contexts have no pending entry after reset. Released read statuses are routed to local readiness or remote replies, and caller-side context plus applied index determine completion; the remote batching identity discrepancy remains unresolved.
